what: Builds table-of-contents rows from the article’s h2 section titles, and like the Now line in a calendar, a red 2px line moves down over the TOC row of the section being read by however much has been read within that section (progress to the next heading) — the current row has a white background. The TOC panel (max 360px) scrolls along to keep the line centered, and when the end of the article enters the screen the line drops 6px and vanishes in .2s. Clicking a row smooth-scrolls to that heading

options.body: CSS selector of the text box to search for the title (inside the panel), default the whole panel
options.heads: Heading css to become the table of contents, default h2
options.at: Distance from the top of the screen treated as the reading position (px), default 0 — the height of a sticky header if there is one
options.--fx-max: Max height of the contents panel (style), default 360px
options.[data-fx-part=box]·[data-fx-part=scroll]: Contents panel and its inner scroll panel
options.[data-fx-part=line]: Current line — color is --kf-danger (accent color if missing)
options.[data-fx-part=list]: Where the table of contents rows go — row ([data-fx-part=item]) is created by the part, .is-fx-on on the current row
